notes: Shapes and statistics are recorded by forward hooks on the real model during this request.
VideoCNN averages its per-frame features over the 8 frames inside VideoCNN.forward, between enc_v.net.4 and enc_v.fc; that step has no module, so no hook.
norm_a / norm_v are Identity and the scale injector is disabled in the baseline.

limitations: Trained from scratch on CREMA-D (actor-disjoint split 64/9/18 actors, 5234/738/1470 clips) only (train split). Held-out joint accuracy on unseen people: 50.8% (test, evaluation-only); chance is 16.7%. Accuracy on your own recordings is unknown and is not measured by anything shown here.
Confidence is not correctness. Calibration error (ECE) of the joint head on validation is 0.050; a high top probability does not make a prediction reliable.

The distribution-shift detector (Mahalanobis distance on encoder representations) is fitted on training data with its threshold set on validation data so about 5% of in-distribution inputs are flagged. Its ability to catch out-of-distribution inputs is unknown: passing it is not evidence of reliability.
The video-only probe is weak: 19.3% test accuracy versus 16.7% chance. Video-only predictions carry little information.
CREMA-D contains acted emotions from 91 actors reading 12 scripted sentences in a studio. Real, spontaneous emotion differs; this is not an emotion-recognition system.
Speech and face checks are heuristics: they reject silence, tones, steady noise and frames without a frontal face in the centre crop, but cannot reliably tell speech from singing or rhythmic music.
This baseline is separate from the paper's forward-only, gradient-only and ordinary scaling conditions; no scaling intervention is applied at inference.
disclaimer: Research prototype. Predictions come from a small model trained from scratch on one dataset; they are not a reliable emotion or action recognizer and must not be used for decisions about people.
